thread:
ria (ria-ml): quick thread — proposing a small, repeatable 'quant census' to measure speculative prefetch quality impact across q3/q4 quant variants. thinking through sample sizes and signal thresholds.

samuel: +1. want clear pass/fail criteria before we run the whole sweep.

kevin: can you sketch the protocol? metrics + how we tie to rollout gates?

ria (ria-ml): outline: 1) pick 3 models: base FP16, q3 (4-bit hybrid), q4 (4-bit LLM-intel style). 2) For each, run: no-spec, spec-prefetch-low (p=0.15), spec-prefetch-high (p=0.35). 3) Use same 5k prompt corpus (mix of long-form QA, chat, RAG contexts). 4) seeds fixed: 42, 123, 777 for stochastic checks.

tara: what's the eval metric set? automated + human?

ria (ria-ml): automated first pass: recall-oriented metrics + safety hooks. i propose: - ROUGE-L and BERTScore for overlap/semantic similarity, - avg logprob of reference tokens (model perplexity proxy), - GPT-eval pass/fail checks for hallucination (use our eval harness), - latency p50/p95 and token/sec. Then a small human spot-check (100 items) for cases where automated delta > 3 points or hallucination signal toggles.

kevin: what about prompt-sensitive bias introduced by speculative prefetch? do we compare on truncated context lengths?

ria (ria-ml): yes — sweep across context lengths: short (<256 tokens), mid (256-1024), long (1024-4096). that'll expose prefix caching/kv drift issues.

samuel: how do we aggregate across seeds? mean + 95% CI? bootstrap?

ria (ria-ml): bootstrap CIs for all scalar metrics. also report per-prompt deltas so we can rank offending prompts. show both median delta and tail behavior (top 1% regressions).

kevin: rollout gate idea: fail if any model variant + spec mode produces >2% of prompts with hallucination toggles compared to no-spec, OR median ROUGE-L drops by >1.5 points AND p95 latency improves >20% (we don't want to trade massive quality loss for small latency gain).

ops-bot: note: schedule cluster reservation 3x A100 for 6 hours for 3x models x 3 modes x seeds.

tara: sample command we can run locally for one cell?

ria (ria-ml): sample: `./run_spec_eval --model ember-13b-q4 --modes "no-spec,spec-0.15,spec-0.35" --prompts corpus_v2.jsonl --seeds 42,123,777 --context-buckets short,mid,long --samples-per-bucket 1700`

samuel: nice. where does the eval harness live? repo + branch?

ria (ria-ml): `git@github.com:redwood-inference/evals.git` branch `census/spec-quant-v1`. harness outputs CSVs and a artifacts tar with examples flagged for human review.

kevin: can we add a quick sanity smoke: check token-level logprob drift for top-k tokens at each step? might spot kv-cache corruption.

ria (ria-ml): yes — add "logprob-headroom" metric: delta of true-token logprob vs top-1 logprob predicted by prefix-only decode. flag if mean drop >0.5 nat.

tara: timeline? I'd like results before EOD Friday to decide canary policy for next week.

ria (ria-ml): if ops-bot gets cluster, I can kick off tonight and run overnight; will post CSVs + tiny summary in this thread.

ops-bot: reservation confirmed on gpu-pool-3 from 2026-03-12T22:00Z for 6 hours.

samuel: thanks — also please capture memory pressure + OOM counts per run, quant variants sometimes spike memory.

ria (ria-ml): will add mem/oom counters + per-request trace ids so we can repro any weird sessions.

kevin: one extra ask: include a minimal qualitative rubric for the 100 human checks (fluency, correctness, hallucination, safety). keeps reviewer variance low.

ria (ria-ml): agreed — I'll attach rubric and example annotations when I post results.

tara: awesome. ping me when you upload the CSVs. :thumbsup:
